notes: - The vault now works with APIs, not just website sign-ins. A person saves any API token in their secure vault — GitHub is the example: they create a personal token on GitHub, paste it into their vault once, and the assistant can then work with their own repositories (list them, search, and more) through api.github.com. New tool vault_api: the server attaches the saved secret to the call as the Authorization header; the assistant itself never sees the secret, one person's entry can never be used by another, and if a service echoes the secret back it is scrubbed from the answer. Username+password entries can be used with basic auth. No admin setup and no app registration is involved — it is the person's own key for their own account, which is how token-style services (GitHub and most APIs) are meant to work.
